text:
Predicates:
Cost(greTest, 205) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test.
Cheaper(205, 300) ::: $205 is cheaper than $300.
ProvidesFinancialAid(ets, x) ::: ETS provides financial aid to x.
Applicant(x, greTest) ::: x is a GRE applicant.
ProveEconomicHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
HasFewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available to them.
LivesWithDadOutOfWork(x) ::: x's dad has been out of work.
ApplyingToTake(x, greTest) ::: x is applying to take the GRE test.
Premises:
Cost(greTest, 205) ∧ Cheaper(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x (ProveEconomicHardship(x) → ProvidesFinancialAid(ets, x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x ((LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ∨ HasFewResources(x)) → ProveEconomicHardship(x)) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
LivesWithDadOutOfWork(tom) ∧ HasFewResources(tom) ::: Tom's dad has been out of work, and Tom has few resources available to him.
ApplyingToTake(tom, greTest) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
ProvidesFinancialAid(ets, tom) ::: ETS provides financial aid to Tom.
